# Annotation Interface Experimental

* * *

[@Documented](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/annotation/Documented.html "annotation interface in java.lang.annotation") [@Retention](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/annotation/Retention.html "annotation interface in java.lang.annotation")([CLASS](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/annotation/RetentionPolicy.html#CLASS)) [@Target](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/annotation/Target.html "annotation interface in java.lang.annotation")({[TYPE](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/annotation/ElementType.html#TYPE),[METHOD](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/annotation/ElementType.html#METHOD),[CONSTRUCTOR](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/annotation/ElementType.html#CONSTRUCTOR),[FIELD](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/annotation/ElementType.html#FIELD)}) public @interface Experimental

Marks the annotated element as experimental, exempt from standard stability guarantees. Both its API and its runtime behavior may change incompatibly or be removed at any time without notice. Mirrors ADK Python's `@experimental`.
